text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.6% today as geopolitical tension in the Middle East escalated—Iran attacked U.S. military sites in Kuwait and struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, raising the specter of supply disruptions. Yet oil prices remained relatively flat (U.S. crude at $89.62/barrel), suggesting markets aren't pricing in major production losses yet, and U.S. refineries running at 95% capacity with ample fuel inventories mean there's no immediate squeeze on supply that would benefit refiner margins.

The stock's broader two-week decline—down 7.4%—fits a pattern where initial geopolitical alarm (which spiked the stock to $414.65 on the 13th) has given way to skepticism that the conflict will meaningfully disrupt global oil flows or refinery profits. Diesel prices hit record highs in the U.K., but that's driven inflation concerns rather than a margin windfall for U.S. refiners.
